tr.td: Primary care visit for breathlessness on exertion and ankle swelling
Two-week heart failure medication safety check, echocardiogram, and cardiology consultation
Three-month heart failure and blood pressure review
Same-day sick visit for a head cold and cough
Treat congestion with furosemide and start empagliflozin for HFpEF; move to as-needed furosemide guided by daily weights once euvolemic
Add low-dose spironolactone for HFpEF with blood pressure above target once potassium and kidney function are stable
Cardiology referral to confirm the diagnosis, review the echocardiogram, and look for specific causes such as amyloidosis or valve disease

Check a basic metabolic panel and magnesium one to two weeks after starting or changing diuretic, SGLT2 inhibitor, or mineralocorticoid antagonist therapy, then every three to six months; KCCQ-12 every three to six months
Daily weights, sodium moderation, a written travel plan for weight gain, and continued daily walking; refer to cardiac rehabilitation if exercise tolerance plateaus
Pneumococcal and RSV vaccination and a yearly high-dose influenza vaccine to lower the risk of respiratory infection in heart failure
Reach euvolemia with no ankle edema and a stable dry weight within three months
Dry weight 56 kg; furosemide changed to as-needed use
Improve the KCCQ-12 overall summary score by at least 15 points by the three-month review
Lower blood pressure below 130/80 by the six-month review without orthostatic symptoms
Blood pressure 126/72; no dizziness on standing
Resume a full speaking and travel schedule by the six-month review
Back to lecturing twice a month with a travel weight plan
